newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST-Skanska '96 profit seen up 90 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Skanska '96 profit seen up 90 pct.

text.p: Swedish construction group Skanska AB was expected on Tuesday to post a profit after financial items including capital gains of 4.93 billion crowns for 1996, a Reuters poll of 12 analysts found on Thursday.
This is an increase of 90 percent compared to 1995 when the company reported a profit of 2.59 billion crowns.
The 1996 profit forecast includes a capital gain of about 1.76 billion crowns for shares sold and 600 million crowns for property sales.
Forecasts varied from 4.40 billion to 5.25 billion crowns.
Analysts estimated sales in 1996 would increase by 21 percent to 46.79 billion crowns.
They forecast a dividend of 5.75 crowns a share compared to 5.00 crowns in 1995.
Profit after financial items in 1997 was expected to be 3.42 billion crowns and for 1998 seen at 3.89 billion crowns.
Analysts interviewed for the poll were from Aros, Alfred Berg, Carnegie, Fiba Nordic, Handelsbanken, James Capel, Kleinwort Benson, Nordiska, Paribas, S-E-Banken, Swedbank and Ohman.
Skanska will present its 1996 earnings on February 25.
